Lalmohan Babu.description: Feluda's friend and a popular writer of thriller stories who uses the pen name Jatayu; his full name is Lalmohan Ganguli.

Feluda.description: A private investigator and the protagonist of the series, also known as Pradosh Mitter and respectfully addressed as Felu Bab.

Sadhan Chakravarty.description: A previous client of Feluda, mentioned as the person who referred Ranjan K. Majumdar.

Mahabharata.description: An ancient Indian epic, often adapted for television and widely known in Indian culture.

Doordarshan.description: India's public service broadcaster, known for airing television serials and news.

Prakhar Rudra.description: A fictional hero created by Lalmohan Babu for his stories.

America.description: Referenced as a country, often contrasted with India in terms of media and entertainment.

Superman.description: A famous American comic book superhero, used here as a reference to casting authenticity.

Bengal.description: A region in eastern India, referenced in the context of finding a suitable actor.

Durga Puja.description: A major Hindu festival celebrated in Bengal and other parts of India, honoring the goddess Durga.

Hindi.description: An Indian language, referenced here in the context of film songs.

England.description: A country in the United Kingdom, where Ranjan K. Majumdar spent part of his youth.

Cambridge.description: A city in England known for its prestigious university, referenced as the location of a college attended by Ranjan.

India.description: The country where the story is set and to which Ranjan returns after his time in England.

St Xavier’s College.description: St Xavier’s College, commonly called St Xavier’s, is a renowned educational institution in Calcutta attended by several characters in the story.

Calcutta.description: The former name of Kolkata, a major city in eastern India.

Delhi.description: The capital city of India, where Ranjan's daughter lives.

Roland Road.description: A street address in Calcutta, given as Ranjan K. Majumdar's residence.

Lee & Watkins.description: The name of the chartered accountancy firm where Ranjan K. Majumdar works.

B. Com.description: Bachelor of Commerce, an undergraduate degree in commerce.

dhoti.description: A traditional Indian garment for men, consisting of a long piece of cloth wrapped around the waist and legs.

kurta.description: A loose, collarless shirt worn in South Asia, often paired with a dhoti or pajamas.

namaskar.description: A respectful greeting in India, similar to 'hello' or 'greetings'.

ayurvedic.description: Relating to Ayurveda, a traditional Indian system of medicine.

Dharani Mukherjee.description: A chartered accountant known to Feluda, who is familiar with Ranjan Majumdar through the Saturday Club.

Ranjan Majumdar.description: A quiet and reserved man central to the investigation who spent part of his life in England; he is the son of Rajani Majumdar.

Dr Hiren Basak.description: A homeopath and former student at St Xavier’s, who is consulted by Feluda regarding the photograph.

Raghunath Majumdar.description: Ranjan Majumdar’s grandfather, described as a former terrorist who fought against the British.

Saturday Club.description: A prestigious social club in Calcutta, frequented by professionals and elites.

Hastings.description: A locality in Calcutta where Dr Jyotirmoy Sen resides.

British.description: Refers to people from Britain, historically significant in the context of Indian independence.

homeopath.description: A practitioner of homeopathy, an alternative system of medicine popular in India.

bearer.description: A domestic servant or attendant, often found in Indian households.

orthodox medicine.description: Conventional or allopathic medicine, as opposed to alternative systems like homeopathy.

John Dexter.description: A tourist from Australia who recognizes his cousin Peter Dexter in a photo and provides information to Feluda.

Peter Dexter.description: John Dexter's first cousin, whose whereabouts are being investigated; son of Michael Dexter.

Michael Dexter.description: Peter Dexter's father, who served in the Indian Army and later returned to England.

George.description: Michael Dexter's eldest son and Peter Dexter's brother, who was also in the army.

Statesman.description: An English-language newspaper published in India, with editions in Delhi and Calcutta.

Grand Hotel.description: A well-known hotel in Calcutta where John Dexter is staying.

Kathmandu.description: The capital city of Nepal, mentioned as John Dexter's next destination.

Australia.description: A country and continent, where John Dexter has lived since leaving England.

Indian Army.description: The land-based branch of the Indian Armed Forces, where Michael Dexter served.

Norfolk.description: A county in England, where Michael Dexter lived after returning from India.

London.description: The capital city of England, where Feluda is advised to continue his investigation.

settee.description: A long upholstered seat for more than one person; a sofa.

UK.description: Short for United Kingdom, the country where the group is traveling for their investigation.

Air-India.description: The national airline of India, which the characters use to fly to London.

Bombay.description: The former name of Mumbai, a major Indian city where the group catches a connecting flight.

Regent Palace.description: The hotel in London where the group is booked to stay.

Piccadilly Circus.description: A famous road junction and public space in London, near their hotel.

Mont Blanc.description: A famous mountain in the Alps, mentioned as visible from the plane.

Heathrow.description: London's main international airport, where the group lands.

almirah.description: A freestanding cupboard or wardrobe, commonly used in Indian households.

Tapesh.description: Feluda's younger cousin and the narrator of the stories, affectionately called Topshe, who assists with investigations and documentation.

Bikash Datta.description: Feluda's friend living in London who provides useful information for the investigation.

Oxford Street.description: A famous and busy shopping street in central London, known for its large stores and crowds.

Marks & Spencer.description: A well-known British multinational retailer with a store on Oxford Street.

Boots.description: A major British pharmacy and retailer chain.

Debenhams.description: A British multinational retailer operating department stores, with a location on Oxford Street.

D. H. Evans.description: A historic department store in London, now part of House of Fraser.

John Lewis.description: A major chain of high-end department stores in the UK.

Selfridges.description: A famous luxury department store located on Oxford Street in London.

Richmond.description: A suburban town in southwest London, where Dr Sen lives.

Piccadilly.description: A major road and area in central London, known for its tube station.

South Kensington.description: A district in West London with a major tube station where the characters change trains.

District Line.description: A line of the London Underground (tube) system.

Babu.description: A respectful Bengali term for 'gentleman' or 'sir', often used as a suffix to names.

GP.description: Short for 'General Practitioner', a common term for a primary care doctor in India and the UK.

Dr Sen.description: An Indian doctor living in Richmond, England, who came as a medical student after World War II and was a former batchmate of Ranjan Majumdar at St Xavier’s.

Emily.description: Dr Sen's English wife, who welcomes the guests and offers them coffee.

Rajani Majumdar.description: Ranjan's father, a doctor who once lived and worked in England before returning to India.

Britain.description: The country where Dr Sen and his family now reside.

St Mary’s Hospital.description: A renowned hospital in London where Rajani Majumdar worked.

Major Barbara.description: A play by George Bernard Shaw, referenced as the play Dr Sen and Rajani Majumdar attended together.

Golders Green.description: A residential area in northwest London where Rajani Majumdar lived.

Hampstead.description: A district of London where Dr Sen lived when he first came to England.

Epping.description: A town in Essex, England, where Warrendel school is located.

Trinity.description: Refers to Trinity College, one of the colleges at the University of Cambridge.

macintoshes.description: Waterproof raincoats, commonly used in British and Indian English.

chartered accountant.description: A professional accountant with certification, a term commonly used in India and the UK.

terrorist.description: In this context, refers to Indian revolutionaries who used violent means against British colonial rule.

Mr Manning.description: A staff member at Warrendel School who assists Feluda in searching the student records.

Warrendel School.description: Warrendel School, often referred to simply as Warrendel, is the fictional school in Epping attended by Ranjan Majumdar.

Times.description: Refers to The Times, a major British newspaper.

Madame Tussaud’s.description: A renowned wax museum in London featuring lifelike wax figures of famous personalities.

Houses of Parliament.description: The seat of the UK Parliament, located in London.

Big Ben.description: The nickname for the Great Bell of the clock at the north end of the Palace of Westminster in London.

St Paul’s Cathedral.description: A famous Anglican cathedral in London, known for its dome.

Baker Street.description: Baker Street is a well-known street in London, famously associated with the fictional address 221-B Baker Street, the residence of Sherlock Holmes.

Sherlock Holmes.description: The legendary fictional detective created by Sir Arthur Conan Doyle.

Conan Doyle.description: Sir Arthur Conan Doyle, the creator of Sherlock Holmes.

Archibald Cripps.description: A visitor who claims to have information about Peter Dexter and displays a brusque, prejudiced attitude.

Reginald.description: The youngest Dexter sibling, currently in India working at a tea estate and suffering from cancer.

Mr Tailor.description: A staff member at Trinity College who has access to old student records.

Hookins.description: The long-serving gardener at Trinity College who witnessed the aftermath of the boating accident.

Sikhs.description: A religious and ethnic group from the Punjab region, known for their martial tradition.

Gurkhas.description: Soldiers from Nepal renowned for their bravery, often serving in the British and Indian armies.

Liverpool Street.description: A major railway station in London.

Chatworth Street.description: A street in Cambridge where Hookins lives.

Maggie.description: Hookins's wife, whom he married on the day of the boating accident.

Satyanathan.description: A South Indian gentleman and teacher in London who provides information about Peter Dexter and Ranjan Majumdar.

Inspector Mandal.description: A police inspector in Calcutta who informs Feluda about Ranjan Majumdar's death.

Kilburn.description: A district in north London where Satyanathan lives.

Whit Sunday.description: A Christian holiday, also known as Pentecost, referenced as the day before Peter Dexter's death.

Sadar Street.description: A street in Calcutta where the hotel is located in which Reginald Dexter commits suicide.

Khoirabari.description: A tea estate near Darjeeling, mentioned as Reginald Dexter's place of origin.

Darjeeling.description: A hill station in India, famous for its tea estates.

Ganesh.description: A Hindu deity with an elephant head, worshipped as the remover of obstacles.
